solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: A godly performing songstress is a protesting female

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters putting on an act and taking a new shape

parts.note: a diva is a celebrated female opera singer

explanation.surface: A pious singer turns out to be a woman on a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges A GODLY into LADYGO. Legend says the Countess Godiva rode naked through Coventry to protest her husband's taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary noblewoman rode unclothed through Coventry in protest at heavy taxes, the most famous female protester of English folklore.

clue.text: Stick commercial notice in this location

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a commercial notice
here means at this place

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put up an advert right on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick and to cling are synonyms for remaining firmly attached.

clue.text: Spends enjoyable time making displays

definitions.meaning: to socialise casually somewhere, relaxing with friends
putting things on show, as washing on a line or flags from a window

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys their leisure arranging exhibitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb has two senses: lounging socially, and literally suspending items so they show.

clue.text: To be in opposition is the thing

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to protest or disagree
as a noun, an article or item

explanation.surface: Opposing something is what matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to protest; as a noun it means a physical item or article.

clue.text: Food from aquatic creatures — is the man catching thousand in Cornish river?

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England

indicators.note: catching means the man holds the next piece within him

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An angler is pictured landing a big haul on a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, England's south-western county; 'the man' is the pronoun he, and 'catching' puts the thousand inside him before it all goes 'in' the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish ground into a meal is used as animal feed and fertiliser, a food made from sea creatures.

clue.text: Piano tune for players of duet?

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A piano melody written for two performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet is played by two people, so the performers form a couple or twosome.

clue.text: Female in the family makes good money having obtained degree

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars, a good sum of money
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A woman earns a big salary after gaining her qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is an older female relative in the family.

clue.text: I'm led astray with disguise that could bring a shattering experience

definitions.text: that could bring a shattering experience

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters leave their order

explanation.surface: Someone misled by a disguise faces a devastating encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges IMLED and DISGUISE together into the thirteen letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steered rocket weapon strikes its target explosively, causing a literally shattering event.

clue.text: Robber in group carrying apparatus

indicators.note: carrying means the group holds the apparatus within it

parts.note: a band is a group of people
a rig is a piece of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: A thief belongs to a gang lugging equipment around.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, an outlaw who robs travellers.

clue.text: Disown someone in care and refuse to admit guilt

definitions.meaning: a charge is a person in one's care, and to deny is to disown
to reject the accusation made against one

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a dependant and pleads innocence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means rejecting an accusation; read literally it means disowning a ward or dependant.

clue.text: I leave guy floundering in a prestigious academic group

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a struggling man at an elite university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floundering' rearranges the letters of I LEAVE GUY.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of eight old, elite universities in the north-east United States carries this name.

clue.text: Injured coming to a premature stop on lake

indicators.note: stopping early means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: hurt means injured
taken as written

explanation.surface: An injured person halts short on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to a premature stop' cuts the final T from HURT to leave HUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Huron is one of the five Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Old group having gone to gym go off to the match?

parts.note: ELO, the Electric Light Orchestra, was a 1970s rock band
PE, physical education, is gym class at school

explanation.surface: A veteran band has left the gym to attend a sports game.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'match' is a marriage, not a game: eloping is running off to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who run away secretly to marry are heading off to their wedding, a match in the marital sense.

clue.text: At a particular place of action without delay

definitions.text: At a particular place of action
definitions.meaning: present at the very scene where something happens

explanation.surface: Someone is at the scene and acts instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means present at the scene, and also immediately.

clue.text: Sort of runner with inner energy who keeps things calm?

indicators.note: with inner means the next piece goes inside the runner

parts.note: a pacemaker is a runner who sets the speed in a race
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A race runner with inner energy turns out to be a calming influence.
explanation.definitionFit: One who keeps calm and settles disputes is a mediator bringing harmony.

clue.text: Detrimental effect this person's found twirling around in tights

indicators.note: twirling around means both pieces are spun so they read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a damaging cost, as in taking its toll
this person is is I am

explanation.surface: A dancer spinning in tights suffers for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling around' reverses both pieces together, giving the letters in the order they are entered. A maillot is a one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a tight-fitting garment worn by dancers and acrobats, covering the legs as hosiery does.

clue.text: Sweet tablet swallowed by Kitty going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the assembled letters are read backwards
swallowed by means the tablet goes inside the kitty

parts.note: a pool is a shared fund of money, a kitty
a pill is a tablet

explanation.surface: A cat chokes on a pill it took down the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' is a shared fund of money, not a cat. 'swallowed by' puts the tablet inside it, making POPILLOL, and 'going the wrong way' turns that whole run around.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard candy on a stick, a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Criminal residing in nasty little community

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: vile means nasty
a lag is a slang term for a convict

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer lives in a horrid small settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A village is a small rural settlement, smaller than a town.

clue.text: Archdeacon American fellow? He's from another planet!

parts.note: an archdeacon is addressed as the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
Ian is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A clergyman from the States is said to be an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England an archdeacon's title is 'the Venerable', shortened to Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the second planet from the sun would be described by this word.

clue.text: Country workers seen as steady and reliable chaps?

definitions.meaning: rural workers who tend horses in stables

definitions.text: seen as steady and reliable chaps?
definitions.meaning: stable means steady, and men are chaps

explanation.surface: Farm hands are regarded as dependable fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooms who look after horses are rural workers; read whimsically, the word describes steady men.

clue.text: Piece of music? It sounds deadly, needing new introduction!

indicators.note: It sounds says the answer is judged by how it is pronounced aloud

parts.note: deadly, said as dedly, with a fresh first letter M in place of its D, is heard as medly

explanation.surface: A tune is described as dreadful and in need of a fresh opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'deadly' as it is pronounced, swap its opening D for M (the 'new introduction'), and the result is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a musical piece stitched from several songs or tunes.

clue.text: European security measure through audio detection

indicators.note: audio detection means the word is identified by listening to its sound

parts.note: a check is a security inspection

explanation.surface: Security is tightened by monitoring sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Czech Republic is a European.

clue.text: Line engineers carried in box

indicators.note: carried in means placed inside the box

parts.note: a case is a box
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers bring in a box full of cables.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line made by folding, as on paper or trousers.

clue.text: One artist facing question, one native of troubled land

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
I again stands for one

explanation.surface: An artist faces a question from a man from a war-torn country.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Iraq, a land long troubled by war.

clue.text: Feature of dream ending — after this there's no more to be said

definitions.text: after this there's no more to be said

indicators.note: Feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dream's finale leaves nothing more to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Said at the end of a prayer, the word closes things off, so nothing follows it.

clue.text: State of collapse could bring new despair to Irish

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A ruin could bring fresh misery to the people of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DESPAIR into DISREPA; 'could bring' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is a run-down condition of buildings falling apart.

clue.text: Problem after too much reading? It doesn't look good

definitions.meaning: read as ..., aching eyes from long reading

explanation.surface: Strained vision is no pretty picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an ugly sight; split, it describes eyes aching from reading.

clue.text: A superior holy person before becoming stern

parts.note: U denotes upper-class, superior
St is short for Saint
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A lofty saint is about to turn severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and stern are synonyms for severe and strict in manner.
